newsitem.title: USA: Oak Industries finds accounting irregularities.
newsitem.headline: Oak Industries finds accounting irregularities.

text.p: Oak Industries Inc., a supplier of communications equipment components, said Monday it had discovered accounting irregularities within its OakGrisgby Inc. unit.
Oak said it has fired the division's controller and two of his assistants, who were not identified, and filed suit against them. Details about the suit were not immediately available.
OakGrigsby, based in Sugar Grove, Ill., produces traditional analogue and digitial switch controls.
Oak said outside legal counsel and independent accountants conducted an investigation, and "confirmed that the accounting irregularities were isolated to this one division."

As a result of the audit, Oak said it has restated its financial results for the first, second and third quarters of 1996. Because the impact on 1995 was not material, the 1995 financial statements were not restated.

Oak, based in Waltham, Mass., also said its net income soared to $9.7 million, or 52 cents per share, in the fourth quarter ended Dec. 31, from $4.2 million, or 23 cents per share, in the year-ago period. Sales grew to $70.1 million from $69.0 million.
Oak's stock fell $1.125 to $19.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
